criteria.name: Mission concept and rationale — What will it do, who are the users, why is it needed?
criteria.reasoning: The need, broad mission function, Australian benefit, and intended users are identifiable, with supporting sources. The concept lacks specific mission requirements and payload or service performance targets, so it is only at the lower end of Accomplished.

evidence.quote: A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events.
This tool could be applied to a new satellite over the Great Barrier Reef.

criteria.name: Project plan — How you plan to complete the assignment, including either a Gantt chart or a timetable and information sources you plan to use
criteria.reasoning: A Gantt chart and task descriptions make the plan broadly feasible and connect planned work to launch, orbit, and mission design. However, contingency planning is absent, some timing descriptions conflict with the chart, and planned information sources are not clearly set out.

evidence.quote: Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart.
Running basic simulations in STK will also be useful.

criteria.name: Preliminary progress — Technical content and evidence of sufficient work done to date
criteria.reasoning: Research and software tutorials constitute some preliminary work, but no useful technical results, calculations, or interpreted simulations are presented. The proposed orbit is technically inconsistent: a 600 km orbit is not geostationary.

evidence.quote: I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4.
My current choice is a geostationary orbit at an altitude of 600 km

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Headings, coherent sections, and a legible labelled Gantt chart support readability. Some phrasing is informal or awkward, and the references are presented as numbered URLs rather than a complete reference list. The plan's prose and chart also have some inconsistencies.

evidence.quote: Coral reefs, specifically the Great Barrier Reef, would immensely benefit from dedicated satellite monitoring.
Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page.

technical_issues.issue: A 600 km altitude orbit cannot be geostationary. Geostationary orbit requires an approximately 35,786 km altitude circular, equatorial orbit with a 24-hour period; a low orbit would not remain fixed over the reef.
The plan says final simulations should be completed by the end of week 9, while the chart shows STK simulations scheduled through week 10.

overall: The report presents a relevant Australian mission concept, a timetable, and evidence of initial research and STK learning. Its main weaknesses are limited preliminary engineering results, incomplete identification of planned information sources, and a fundamental error in the proposed orbit. The mission concept is promising but needs quantified requirements and a feasible orbit strategy.

feedback.summary: You present a relevant Australian mission concept, a readable report structure and timetable, and evidence of initial research and STK learning. To reach the next rubric level, strengthen the concept with measurable requirements, make the project plan more robust and consistent, and include preliminary engineering results that support a technically feasible mission.
next_steps: In Mission Concept & Rationale, turn the broad goal of near-real-time reef monitoring into measurable requirements—for example, specify coverage, revisit or latency needs, and payload or service performance targets. Connect each target to the needs of marine and conservation scientists, and support the choices with appropriate sources.

In Project Plan & Preliminary Progress, correct the orbit concept: a 600 km orbit is not geostationary and cannot remain fixed over the reef. Assess feasible orbit options against your coverage and latency requirements. Also reconcile the week 9 simulation deadline with the chart’s week 10 schedule, add contingency time, and identify the information sources you will use.

To move C3 beyond Adequate, go beyond research and tutorials by presenting initial calculations or simulation outputs, briefly interpreting what they show, and explaining how they inform the mission design. For C4, use more formal phrasing and provide a complete, consistently formatted reference list that matches your in-text citations.

criteria.C1: You identify the Australian benefit, broad mission function and intended users, and support the concept with sources. To strengthen this Accomplished result, define specific mission requirements and payload or service performance targets tied to user needs.
criteria.C2: Your Gantt chart and task descriptions make the plan broadly feasible and relate work to mission design. To reach Accomplished, specify planned information sources, add contingencies, explain the schedule in relation to the mission, and resolve the week 9 versus week 10 simulation timing conflict.
criteria.C3: Your background research and STK tutorials show initial progress. To reach Accomplished, include useful technical results—such as calculations or interpreted simulations. Correct the proposed 600 km geostationary orbit: geostationary orbit requires approximately 35,786 km altitude and a 24-hour period.
criteria.C4: Headings, coherent sections and a labelled Gantt chart help readability. To reach Accomplished, improve formal phrasing, make the prose and chart consistent, and provide complete, consistently formatted references that match citations in the text.
